_comment: HS Phase 8 benchmark — excavation unload in OC clay. Reference: standard excavation/heave benchmark — see Plaxis 'Excavation in over-consolidated clay' or equivalent. The excavated region is modeled by applying an upward (negative-direction) surface traction equal to the removed-overburden pressure on the excavation footprint. The remaining soil rebounds via the HS unload modulus E_ur. True staged construction (geostatic phase → excavation phase) is out of Phase 8 scope; this fixture is single-phase analysis. Stiff OC clay (OCR=2) under small unloads is in the strict elastic regime — most GPs stay elastic (cap is ahead of K0 state), and heave is a clean linear-elastic rebound. The applied unload is kept small (10 kPa rather than the full 90 kPa) to stay within the HS Newton's robust regime for the OCR=2 stiff-clay parameter point.
name: hs_oc_excavation
description: Excavation-style unload on over-consolidated stiff clay (OCR = 2).

excavation._note: Asymmetric excavation footprints (x ∈ [0, 4] m partial unload) trigger HS Newton divergence per § B.9; Phase 8 instead applies UNIFORM unload across the full top edge to model the average overburden removal. Heave is mean-uniform — equivalent to the cross-sectional average heave of a wider excavation.

loading._note: Uniform upward (unload) pressure: -10 kPa across the full top edge. The HS dispatcher at OCR=2, low unload, uniform loading remains in the strict elastic regime where most GPs stay below cone and cap, ensuring robust Newton convergence at full λ.

initialStress._note: Mid-depth confining stress σ_v=100 kPa simulates in-situ K0 state in OC clay before unloading.

heaveMagnitudeAtBase.description: Heave order: at the 10 kPa uniform unload, the OC stiff-clay rebound on a 10m × 8m block is around 0.5-2 mm. Band is generous (10 μm to 5 cm) to cover variations in mesh and load level.

expected.heaveSign: positive (upward) at the top surface under unload.
